# Example data (aggregated particle number concentrations, SMEAR I Varrio forest)

An already-aggregated seven-column version of
[`data`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/data.md).
The 61 size bins of the raw size distribution have been collapsed into
three log-normal modes (nucleation, Aitken, accumulation) plus two total
concentrations (`tconc`, `TPNC`). The dataset covers the same two-month
window as `data` (January and July 2020) and is intended for read-only
demos.

## Usage

``` r
data1
```

## Format

A data frame with 7,640 observations on the following 7 variables.

- `date`:

  a POSIXct vector, sampling time (10-minute resolution).

- `monthyear`:

  a character vector, e.g. `"January 2020"`.

- `Nucleation`:

  a numeric vector, number concentration in the nucleation mode
  (nominally 3–25 nm).

- `Aitken`:

  a numeric vector, number concentration in the Aitken mode (nominally
  25–100 nm).

- `Accumulation`:

  a numeric vector, number concentration in the accumulation mode
  (nominally 100–1000 nm).

- `tconc`:

  a numeric vector, total number concentration.

- `TPNC`:

  a numeric vector, total particle number concentration.

## Details

Unlike
[`data`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/data.md),
which is the raw size-resolved table, `data1` contains only
mode-integrated values. The three integrated values can remain non-zero
even when the smallest raw size bins (`1` through `2`) are entirely `NA`
in the two-month subset. It has:

- very few missing values,

- no long consecutive missing runs,

- no obvious outliers.

Because of this, `data1` is **not** a useful input for the cleaning
pipeline
([`varidele`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/varidele.md),
[`obsedele`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/obsedele.md),
[`condextr`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/condextr.md),
[`shorvalu`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/shorvalu.md),
[`dataprep`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/dataprep.md)):
those steps have nothing to remove on an already-clean table. It is
intended for demos that only read the data:

- [`descdata`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/descdata.md)
  /
  [`descplot`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/descplot.md)
  — descriptive statistics and plots,

- [`percdata`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/percdata.md)
  /
  [`percplot`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/percplot.md)
  — percentile summaries,

- [`na_diagnose`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/na_diagnose.md)
  — missing-value diagnostics,

- [`data_report`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/data_report.md)
  — compact quality report.

Use
[`data`](https://chunshengliang.github.io/dataprep/reference/data.md)
for anything that modifies values.

## Source

<https://smear.avaa.csc.fi/download>

## References

Liang, C.-S., Wu, H., Li, H.-Y., Zhang, Q., Li, Z. & He, K.-B. (2020).
Efficient data preprocessing, episode classification, and source
apportionment of particle number concentrations. *Science of the Total
Environment*, 741, 140923.
[doi:10.1016/j.scitotenv.2020.140923](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2020.140923)
